misconceptions.description: Believing one end-of-sprint deadline is sufficient to facilitate asynchronous design work
misconceptions.trigger: learner plans only a final upload with no intermediate checkpoints for distributed students
misconceptions.feedback: Distribute checkpoints (skeleton, signaling pass, final) so stalled work surfaces early instead of all reasoning bursting at the deadline.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a live meeting is the only way to give just-in-time studio feedback
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes scheduling a synchronous session to fix an asynchronous facilitation gap
misconceptions.feedback: Asynchronous facilitation needs visible artifacts and targeted async support moves, not a synchronous fallback that excludes off-hours learners.

misconceptions.description: Tagging a whole storyboard as confusing instead of naming the specific frame and decision
misconceptions.trigger: stuck-note points to the entire artifact rather than one frame and one unresolved decision
misconceptions.feedback: Pin the stuck-note to one frame and the exact decision you cannot resolve so the reply targets that frame.

misconceptions.description: Believing that more announcements, reminders, and nudges facilitate an asynchronous cohort, when volume raises transactional pressure without lowering transactional distance.
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes adding reminders or automated check-in emails instead of observation points
misconceptions.feedback: A reminder raises pressure; it does not change what the facilitator can see or when. Lower transactional distance by tuning structure: spaced checkpoints, a stuck-note channel, and public process create observation points where contingent help can land. Add a checkpoint, not more nudges.
